title: Unified Behavioral Intelligence Curriculum (6MX + Ellipsis Manual) — Tier 2 Bundle

Signal/Indicator.definition: Externally observable, timestamped behavioral data (somatic cue, vocal shift, linguistic marker, facial movement). Must be visible or audible on camera.

Internal State/Driver.definition: Unobservable psychological motive, fear, autonomic arousal state, or identity construct inferred from signals. Never treated as direct fact without confirmation.

Cognitive Mechanism.definition: Underlying information-processing rule, attentional filter, or decision architecture that converts inputs into internal shifts or behavior.

Tactical Lever.definition: Deliberate operator adjustment—postural, framing, questioning, or structural—deployed to gather information, stabilize rapport, or shift compliance.

Failure Mode.definition: Diagnostic error, false positive, operator bias, or second-order relational blowback that corrupts accuracy or breaks trust.

operator-baseline.definition: The practitioner's calibrated emotional, postural, and attentional neutrality prior to contact; prevents operator noise from distorting subject telemetry.

the-four-lenses.definition: Sequential perceptual filter (Broken -> Different -> Facts -> Reasons) used to strip moral judgment and isolate causal behavior.

observer-distortion.definition: Contamination of a subject's natural baseline caused by the operator's own anxiety, dominance overplay, or visible scrutiny.

hypothesis-plurality.definition: Holding two or more competing Lens 4 causal explanations in suspension until an active probe yields disconfirming or confirming data.

autonomic-decay-lag.definition: The physiological braking time (typically 45-90 seconds) required for sympathetic constriction to subside after a stressor or Observer Distortion is removed.

exogenous-noise.definition: Behavioral constriction or distraction caused by factors outside the interaction (illness, temperature, prior events) that mimics stimulus-linked stress.

authority-architecture.definition: Deliberate calibration of physical presence, vocal cadence, non-reactivity, and spatial command that lowers a subject's resistance threshold and stabilizes compliance.

first-contact-frame.definition: The implicit social hierarchy and relational expectations established in the opening 30-90 seconds of an interaction.

dominance-overplay.definition: Confusing loud aggression, rigid posturing, or territorial hostility with authority; triggers immediate Observer Distortion and defensive armor.

subject-baseline.definition: A subject's normal, low-stress spectrum of posture, blink rate, vocal pitch, and gesture cadence established in neutral conversation before any high-stakes stimulus is introduced.

btoe-stress-cluster.definition: Three or more kinematically independent somatic indicators from the Behavioral Table of Elements (weighted on the 1.0-4.0 severity scale) firing within a 3-5 second window immediately following a specific conversational stimulus.

autonomic-pacifier.definition: Self-soothing tactile behavior (neck touch, leg rubbing, arm wrap, lip compression, ventilated collar tug) triggered by sympathetic nervous system arousal to bleed off internal pressure.

single-cue-fallacy.definition: Treating one isolated gesture (e.g., crossed arms, nose touch, or gaze shift) as proof of stress, resistance, or deception without baseline comparison or multi-channel clustering.

cognitive-baseline.definition: A subject's normal somatic and ocular shift under neutral, effortful thinking—logged separately from their casual rapport baseline to prevent mental-effort false positives.

kinematic-independence.definition: Validation rule requiring cues inside a BToE Stress Cluster to be physiologically distinct autonomic vents rather than sub-parts of one mechanical posture adjustment.

othello-error.definition: Misinterpreting a truth-teller's autonomic stress (caused by fear of disbelief or blame) as proof of deception.

expression-stop-vs-fade.definition: Temporal decay signature of a facial display: authentic emotions dissipate organically as autonomic arousal subsides (fade), whereas consciously performed expressions terminate abruptly once their social purpose is served (stop).

microexpression-leakage.definition: Brief, involuntary facial muscle contraction (typically lasting a fraction of a second) that flashes across the face before conscious executive control clamps the social mask back into place.

artificial-smile.definition: A manually recruited lower-face smile (zygomaticus pull) lacking involuntary upper-face engagement around the eyes (orbicularis oculi), often paired with asymmetric timing or an abrupt stop.

fabrication-marker.definition: Convergent facial, ocular, and narrative-delivery shifts (rehearsed cadence, sensory-detail drop, incongruent emotional timing, or asymmetric display) hypothesized to distinguish constructed accounts from recalled memory.

landing-window-attention.definition: Placing a high-salience phrase at the end of a short prompt and going completely silent so operator visual bandwidth is free to observe the immediate 1-second autonomic response.

social-transition-cutoff.definition: Misreading an abrupt drop in facial expression caused by normal cognitive task-switching (e.g., looking at a screen or notes) as a performed Expression Stop.

rehearsed-truth-artifact.definition: Misclassifying a genuine, truthful account that has been polished through repeated retelling as a constructed Fabrication Marker.

primary-social-need.definition: The dominant social currency a subject prioritizes (Significance, Approval, Acceptance, Intelligence, Pity, Strength/Power) to stabilize self-worth.

hidden-fear-map.definition: The inverse shadow of a Primary Social Need—the specific vulnerability or status loss the subject actively defends against.

six-minute-loop.definition: Iterative diagnostic cycle moving from Visual Phase (passive intake) to Verbal Phase (targeted probing) to live hypothesis updating.

protective-mask.definition: Habitual social persona projected to secure a Primary Social Need while concealing the underlying Hidden Fear Map.

elicitation-probe.definition: Low-friction conversational prompt designed to draw out unguarded data without triggering interrogation alarms.

psychological-reactance.definition: Defensive pushback triggered when a subject perceives their autonomy is being cornered, instantly collapsing rapport and compliance.

tiers.title: The Sensory Layer (Nonverbal & Stress Telemetry)
tiers.subtitle: Building the high-resolution instrument panel for reading autonomic stress, cognitive load, and baseline deviation.

M03.title: The Behavioral Table of Elements (BToE)
M03.canonicalFocus: Reading somatic stress clusters across the 1.0-4.0 severity scale without falling for single-cue myths.

sixMinuteXRayChapters: Ch. 3-4: The Behavioral Table of Elements, Color-Coded Channels, Gesture Types, Postural Barriers, & Baseline Rules
ellipsisManualChapters: Ch. 2: BToE Operational Deployment & Stimulus-Linked Stress Mapping
convergences: Both texts treat the human body as an involuntary telemetry panel wired to the autonomic nervous system, enforcing one hard rule: no single behavior means anything in isolation. Meaning emerges only from a baseline delta confirmed by a multi-cue cluster.
extensions: 6MX builds the encyclopedic diagnostic taxonomy (color-coded anatomical channels and 1.0-4.0 weights); EM turns that static table into a live targeting instrument paired with 3-5 second conversational trigger windows.
tensionsOrContradictions: 6MX occasionally leans toward categorizing high-score BToE clusters as direct deception indicators, whereas EM requires treating them strictly as autonomic stress spikes demanding further probing. Reconciled by locking BToE strictly as a stress-load gauge, never a standalone lie detector.

mentalModel.structuralMetaphorName: The Suspension Bridge Load Telemetry Panel
mentalModel.proseMarkdown:
A suspension bridge never announces that a cable is about to snap with a single loud bang. Under normal traffic, the steel hums, sways, and settles in a steady, predictable rhythm—that ambient motion is its **Subject Baseline**. Engineers do not panic when one bolt creaks in the wind; they watch the **distributed load gauges**. Only when three separate strain sensors—tower deflection, cable tension, and deck vibration—spike in unison the exact second a heavy truck crosses span four do they know the structure is absorbing real stress at a specific coordinate.

The Behavioral Table of Elements (BToE) is that distributed telemetry panel mapped onto the human body. Built directly atop the calm, low-threat room established by **Operator Baseline** (M01) and **Authority Architecture** (M02), the BToE organizes observable human movement into anatomical channels—eyes, face, neck, hands, torso, feet—and assigns each cue a structural load weight from **1.0** (light friction) to **4.0** (acute autonomic strain).

The amateur makes the fatal mistake of treating body language like a dictionary (*crossed arms = defensive; eye rub = lying*). The operator treats it like **hydraulic pressure**. When a conversational stimulus hits a sensitive internal nerve, the sympathetic nervous system surges. Because social norms forbid the subject from fleeing the chair, that excess pressure has to vent somewhere—leaking out as an **Autonomic Pacifier**, a sudden postural barrier, or a freeze in normal gesture cadence. A single creak is noise (**Single-Cue Fallacy**). Three gauges spiking simultaneously within five seconds of a specific question is a **BToE Stress Cluster**—a glowing coordinate on the map telling you *exactly* where the hidden load lives.

granularMechanics.causalChainsMarkdown:
### Mechanism A: Zeroing the Bridge (Subject Baseline & Cognitive Baseline)
`Neutral, low-stakes opening conversation (2-3 minutes)` -> `Operator logs resting posture, blink cadence, hand-gesture amplitude, and vocal tempo` -> `Subject Baseline locked` -> `All subsequent BToE cues are scored strictly as deltas (deviations) from that personal zero-point`.

A single zero-point is never enough. A bridge hums at one frequency under empty lanes and at a completely different frequency under normal commuter traffic. Before you score a single stress cluster, you must log two baselines: the **rapport baseline** (how they move during effortless small talk) and the **Cognitive Baseline** (how their posture, eyes, and hands shift when they are simply thinking hard about a neutral, complex problem). Only a deviation that spikes *above* their Cognitive Baseline counts as genuine autonomic load.

*Micro-Scenario:* During the first three minutes of a vendor negotiation, the opposing lead taps his pen rhythmically and sits with ankles crossed while chatting about his flight. Ten minutes later, when asked about delivery penalties, his hand stops tapping dead, fingers flatten onto the table, and blink rate freezes—a high-contrast freeze delta against his personal baseline. [L2-HOOK:L2-M03-baseline-delta-freeze]

### Mechanism B: Channel Architecture & The BToE Stress Cluster Threshold
The BToE organizes somatic cues into anatomical channels weighted by autonomic energy:
- **Low-Weight Cues (1.0-1.5):** Mild blink-rate shifts, brief lip compression, slight foot angle change.
- **Mid-Weight Cues (2.0-2.5):** **Autonomic Pacifier** behaviors (neck stroke, thigh rub, suprasternal notch touch) and partial barriers (*Single-Arm Wrap*).
- **High-Weight Cues (3.0-4.0):** Full structural shielding (*Fig Leaf*, full torso pivot away, vocal pitch constriction, collar ventilation).

A valid **BToE Stress Cluster** fires only when **three or more distinct indicators** (typically totaling 6.0+ across at least two anatomical channels) erupt inside a **3-to-5-second window** following a specific prompt.

Guard against mechanical double-counting. One physical adjustment—such as leaning back to get comfortable in a stiff chair—naturally drags the torso, arms, and feet along for the ride. For a cluster to clear the threshold, its indicators must satisfy **Kinematic Independence**: separate autonomic vents firing in parallel (such as a sudden lip compression paired with a neck pacifier and a vocal pitch drop), not three angles of the exact same chair shift.

*Micro-Scenario:* Asking a project lead whether QA signed off on the security patch triggers a sharp inhale, *Single-Arm Wrap*, lip disappearance, and a 20-degree torso pivot within four seconds—a confirmed **BToE Stress Cluster** pinned to *QA security sign-off*. [L2-HOOK:L2-M03-cluster-scoring-threshold]

### Mechanism C: Stimulus-to-Spike Mapping & The Single-Cue Fallacy
`Specific verbal stimulus lands` -> `3-5 second latency window` -> `BToE Stress Cluster fires` -> `Operator holds Hypothesis Plurality (M01) and marks the exact phrase` -> `Operator drops a neutral follow-up probe to isolate the root cause`.

Reacting to one isolated cue outside a cluster or 3-5 second window commits the **Single-Cue Fallacy**, as physiology, room temperature, and physical comfort generate constant **Exogenous Noise** (M01). [L2-HOOK:L2-M03-single-cue-trap]

sensorToActuatorLoops.title: Two-Tier Baseline Lock-In
sensorToActuatorLoops.sensorInput: Subject's resting posture, gesture speed, and blink rhythm during 2-3 minutes of safe rapport, followed by a neutral complex question.
sensorToActuatorLoops.interpreterHypothesis: Both Subject Baseline and Cognitive Baseline are stable; Observer Distortion is low.
sensorToActuatorLoops.actuatorCalibration: Transition smoothly from neutral small talk to the first substantive agenda topic without changing vocal tempo.
sensorToActuatorLoops.feedbackSignal: Subject's posture remains steady on neutral topics, confirming a clean zero-point.

sensorToActuatorLoops.title: Spike Pinpointing & Seamless Return Pass
sensorToActuatorLoops.sensorInput: BToE Stress Cluster (3+ kinematically independent cues across 2+ channels) fires within 4 seconds of a specific topic or name.
sensorToActuatorLoops.interpreterHypothesis: Acute autonomic load linked to that exact coordinate (hold Hypothesis Plurality: concealment, fear of blame, or unresolved friction).
sensorToActuatorLoops.actuatorCalibration: Do not confront or stare. Keep Operator Baseline flat, move briefly to a safe topic to let Autonomic Decay Lag (45-90s) clear, then circle back seamlessly from a low-threat angle.
sensorToActuatorLoops.feedbackSignal: The return pass only validates the coordinate if your re-entry is seamless and low-threat—if the cluster re-spikes without operator intensity, the coordinate is confirmed for M08 elicitation.

gradedClaims.claimSummary: Comparing a subject against their own low-stress Subject Baseline and Cognitive Baseline is required for valid behavioral assessment.
gradedClaims.rationale: Individual behavioral variance is massive; personal baseline deltas are foundational in behavioral science.

gradedClaims.claimSummary: Tactile self-soothing (Autonomic Pacifier) increases measurably under acute psychological stress and high cognitive load.
gradedClaims.rationale: Well-documented physiological down-regulation response under sympathetic arousal.

gradedClaims.claimSummary: Isolated single nonverbal gestures (Single-Cue Fallacy) are statistically indistinguishable from chance as indicators of internal states.
gradedClaims.rationale: Confirmed by large-scale deception and nonverbal meta-analyses.

gradedClaims.claimSummary: BToE 1.0-4.0 decimal severity weights prioritize somatic shifts in real time.
gradedClaims.rationale: Practical triage heuristic aligning with Signal Detection Theory's multi-cue logic, though exact decimal weights are not psychometrically validated constants.

gradedClaims.claimSummary: Postural barriers and lower-body escape vectors correlate with discomfort or desire to disengage.
gradedClaims.rationale: Useful immediacy signal when filtered against ergonomics, seating layout, and room temperature.

gradedClaims.claimSummary: High-scoring BToE Stress Clusters serve as direct proof of deception.
gradedClaims.rationale: Collapses under empirical scrutiny due to the Othello Error—truth-tellers under blame pressure emit identical stress clusters.

gradedClaims.claimSummary: Rigid universal gesture dictionaries or NLP eye-accessing cues map 1:1 to fixed psychological meanings across individuals.
gradedClaims.rationale: Repeatedly falsified in controlled meta-analyses of nonverbal deception.

commonMisconceptions: Pinocchio's Nose Misconception: believing BToE is a human polygraph rather than a stress-load coordinate gauge.
Freeze Blindness Trap: scanning only for added fidgeting while missing an animated subject suddenly going statue-still.
highProbabilityFalsePositives: Double-counting one mechanical chair adjustment as three separate BToE indicators (violating Kinematic Independence).
Mistaking normal mental-effort stillness (Cognitive Baseline) or room chill (Exogenous Noise) for autonomic threat.
disconfirmingEvidenceRules: If a suspected stress cue persists unchanged across both sensitive and completely neutral topics—or disappears immediately when the room warms up or the subject shifts chairs—the hypothesis of stimulus-linked stress is falsified (Exogenous Noise).

secondOrder: Staring visibly at a subject's hands, neck, or feet while tallying BToE scores breaks Operator Baseline (M01) and manufactures Observer Distortion—generating artificial Autonomic Pacifier cues.
thirdOrder: Confronting a colleague as dishonest based on an unverified stress cluster triggers the Othello Error and permanent Psychological Reactance (M10).

workedExample.setting: Vendor contract renewal meeting with an account executive.
workedExample.sceneMarkdown: During five minutes of travel talk and standard feature upgrades, the rep gestures broadly and taps his pen lightly while thinking. When asked how regional-node uptime SLA penalties trigger, his pen stops dead mid-tap, palms flatten onto the table, blink rate halts for 4 seconds, and shoulders lock square.

ctaLoop.baseline: High-amplitude gestures, rhythmic pen-tapping, fluid posture across both rapport and moderate cognitive load.
ctaLoop.deviationOrCluster: Abrupt pen-tap halt + palms-flat table lock + 4-second ocular freeze + shoulder rigidity within 2 seconds of 'uptime SLA penalties.'
ctaLoop.internalDriverHypothesis: Hypothesis Plurality: (A) New contract quietly weakened the SLA penalty clause; OR (B) He doesn't know the exact legal trigger and fears looking incompetent.
ctaLoop.tacticalProbeOrActuator: Maintain Operator Baseline and offer a face-saving exit: 'I know the legal appendix gets buried—do we need to pull up Section 4 together, or did that language change from last year?'
ctaLoop.observableFeedbackAndNextMove: Shoulders drop, he exhales, and admits legal revised the regional threshold this quarter before pulling up the redline.

deceptiveNonExample.mirrorSceneMarkdown: Asked to calculate a prorated credit for a mid-quarter seat reduction across three billing tiers, his pen stops tapping, hands go still, and eyes lock on a blank wall spot for 5 seconds.
deceptiveNonExample.benignRootCause: Working-memory saturation (Cognitive Baseline during mental arithmetic) shutting down motor idling to free executive bandwidth.
deceptiveNonExample.disconfirmingCue: Zero accompanying Autonomic Pacifier, lip compression, or torso withdrawal; normal gestures resume immediately upon finishing the math without Autonomic Decay Lag.
deceptiveNonExample.falsePositiveCost: Probing for non-existent pricing traps wastes time and signals unfounded distrust.

L2-M03-cluster-scoring-threshold.operationalFocus: Distinguishing a kinematically independent BToE Stress Cluster (3+ cues, 2+ channels, 3-5s window) from a single mechanical posture shift.

workedExample.setting: Pre-launch readiness review with a product engineering lead.
workedExample.sceneMarkdown: Asked calmly if QA signed off on the third-party auth patch, within 4 seconds she takes a sharp audible inhale, grips her opposite forearm (Single-Arm Wrap), pulls lips inward, and angles her torso 20 degrees toward the door before saying, 'Yeah, we're basically green.'

ctaLoop.baseline: Relaxed shoulders, open torso facing table, fluid cadence across earlier technical reviews.
ctaLoop.deviationOrCluster: Four kinematically independent cues across three channels (respiratory/facial, arm barrier, torso escape vector) within 4 seconds of 'QA signed off.'
ctaLoop.internalDriverHypothesis: Acute load on QA sign-off—partial build sign-off or informally waived edge case.
ctaLoop.tacticalProbeOrActuator: Keep vocal tempo flat, move to a safe topic (launch-day support roster) for 60s to clear Autonomic Decay Lag, then circle back seamlessly asking about any 'monitor post-launch' edge cases.
ctaLoop.observableFeedbackAndNextMove: She relaxes her grip and reveals mobile Safari SSO failed a staging test and awaits a hotfix.

deceptiveNonExample.setting: Identical pre-launch review in a cramped conference room.
deceptiveNonExample.mirrorSceneMarkdown: Asked about QA sign-off, within 3 seconds she pivots her torso 25 degrees left, brings her right arm across her body, and shifts her feet away.
deceptiveNonExample.benignRootCause: Kinematically linked comfort adjustment—reaching across to pull her cardigan tighter against a cold AC vent while shifting off a hard chair edge.
deceptiveNonExample.disconfirmingCue: All three movements are one mechanical reach; face stays relaxed, vocal cadence steady, and she offers unprompted QA ticket IDs.
deceptiveNonExample.falsePositiveCost: Double-counting a physical reach wastes leadership bandwidth auditing a clean component.

L2-M03-single-cue-trap.operationalFocus: Resisting the Single-Cue Fallacy when a classic gesture fires in isolation without overlooking genuine clusters.

workedExample.setting: Performance calibration meeting with a peer manager discussing headcount.
workedExample.sceneMarkdown: While you outline a split of two open roles, your peer crosses his arms tightly and rubs the bridge of his nose, while eye contact, vocal warmth, leaning-in angle, and follow-up questions remain aligned with Subject Baseline.

ctaLoop.baseline: Engaged, collaborative, steady eye contact, open vocal tone.
ctaLoop.deviationOrCluster: Only two isolated low/mid cues with zero facial tension, vocal constriction, or temporal stimulus lock—fails cluster threshold.
ctaLoop.internalDriverHypothesis: Exogenous Noise (room chill, screen eye strain, or comfortable listening posture).
ctaLoop.tacticalProbeOrActuator: Log nothing; continue the proposal normally without asking 'Are you feeling defensive?'
ctaLoop.observableFeedbackAndNextMove: Peer enthusiastically endorses the split and volunteers to draft the job description.

deceptiveNonExample.mirrorSceneMarkdown: Peer crosses arms and you dismiss it as 'just a single-cue myth,' missing that at the exact same second his jaw clenched, blink rate tripled, and answers shrank to clipped two-word nods.
deceptiveNonExample.benignRootCause: Operator error: over-correcting against Single-Cue Fallacy by ignoring concurrent multi-channel telemetry.
deceptiveNonExample.disconfirmingCue: Arm cross was paired with jaw tension, ocular acceleration, and verbal constriction locked to the headcount split.
deceptiveNonExample.falsePositiveCost: Missing a genuine cluster lets silent resentment fester until your peer blocks the requisition with Finance.

L3-M03-btoe-scoring-validity.topicTitle: BToE Numerical Weighting vs. Signal Detection Theory
L3-M03-btoe-scoring-validity.externalScienceMarkdown: The BToE's 1.0-4.0 decimal weights and color-coded taxonomy are an original practitioner framework, not a psychometrically validated instrument with peer-reviewed inter-rater reliability. However, requiring multi-channel convergence and baseline comparison aligns directly with **Signal Detection Theory** (Green & Swets) and clinical coding systems like Ekman & Friesen's **FACS**.
L3-M03-btoe-scoring-validity.operationalTranslation: Use the 1.0-4.0 weights as a fast triage heuristic to organize attention under pressure—never treat a score of '6.5' as an objective mathematical measurement.
keyReferences: Green & Swets (1966) Signal Detection Theory and Psychophysics

L3-M03-postural-barriers-context.topicTitle: Postural Barriers vs. Ergonomic & Environmental Variance
L3-M03-postural-barriers-context.externalScienceMarkdown: Social psychology confirms subtle adjustments in interpersonal immediacy (Mehrabian) under discomfort or affiliation, but naturalistic studies show **ergonomics, thermal comfort, seating geometry, and personal habit** explain a massive share of arm-crossing and foot-angling variance.
L3-M03-postural-barriers-context.operationalTranslation: Always scan chair geometry, table legs, and room temperature before logging a torso pivot or arm wrap as a psychological barrier.

L3-M03-stress-vs-deception-myth.topicTitle: Autonomic Stress Clusters vs. Deception (The Othello Error)
L3-M03-stress-vs-deception-myth.externalScienceMarkdown: Decades of deception research (Aldert Vrij; Ekman's **Othello Error**) conclusively refute that autonomic stress clusters reliably identify lying. Truth-tellers who fear disbelief, embarrassment, or blame exhibit identical sympathetic arousal as deceivers, while practiced liars often show minimal autonomic stress.
L3-M03-stress-vs-deception-myth.operationalTranslation: Discard 'deception detection' and lock strictly onto 'stress mapping'—treat every BToE Stress Cluster as a topic-salience coordinate guiding your next low-threat question.

L3-M03-nonverbal-deception-meta-analysis.externalScienceMarkdown: Landmark meta-analyses (DePaulo et al., 2003; Bond & DePaulo, 2006) established that human accuracy at detecting lies from nonverbal cues hovers around **54%**—barely above chance—with no universal Pinocchio cue across individuals or cultures. NLP eye-accessing charts have been repeatedly falsified (Wiseman et al., 2012).
L3-M03-nonverbal-deception-meta-analysis.operationalTranslation: Discard rigid gesture dictionaries and gaze-direction myths; rely strictly on personal baseline deltas paired with verbal and contextual verification.
keyReferences: DePaulo et al. (2003) Cues to Deception

mentalModel.structuralMetaphorName: The Dual-Rigged Stage Curtain (Hydraulics vs. Manual Strings)
mentalModel.proseMarkdown:
Think of the human face as a stage curtain rigged to two completely separate power sources. Behind the curtain sits a **hydraulic system**—the autonomic nervous system. When real emotion fires, hydraulic pressure surges evenly through both sides of the face, lifting the curtain smoothly, recruiting the involuntary muscles around the eyes, and slowly bleeding off pressure so the expression *fades* like a dimming lamp. In front of the curtain sits **manual rigging**—the conscious motor cortex pulling strings to perform politeness, confidence, or innocence on command.

Manual rigging is clumsy compared to hydraulics. Because conscious control has to *decide* when to pull the strings and when to drop them, performed expressions leave mechanical seams everywhere. They fire a fraction of a second too late, pull unevenly across the left and right hemispheres (asymmetry), miss the deep involuntary eye-ring muscles (**Artificial Smile**), and—most tellingly—drop dead the instant the subject thinks the audience is satisfied (**Expression Stop vs. Fade**).

When a subject is under pressure to conceal an emotion or deliver a constructed story, both systems fight for the same curtain at once. The hydraulic surge fires first, flashing a split-second **Microexpression Leakage** across the brow, lips, or nostrils before the manual rigging slams the polite mask back down. Reading the face is therefore not about memorizing cartoon expressions; it is about watching the *physics of the transition*—spotting where smooth hydraulic motion gets hijacked by jerky manual strings.

granularMechanics.causalChainsMarkdown:
### Mechanism A: Timing & Symmetry (Expression Stop vs. Fade)
`Conscious decision to display emotion` -> `Manual cortical recruitment of lower-face muscles` -> `Asymmetric pull + absence of upper-face contraction` -> `Social goal met` -> `Abrupt release ('Stop') back to flat neutral`.

Context governs the decay curve. An abrupt *stop* is only a mechanical seam when the social beat is still open—such as a grin dying the instant a subject thinks your gaze has moved away. If a person's smile drops cleanly because they immediately pivot their focus into reading a complex document or typing a note, you are watching normal cognitive task-switching (**Social-Transition Cutoff**), not a dropped mask.

*Micro-Scenario:* Informed of an upcoming invoice audit, a department head holds a wide grin (*'Always happy to have fresh eyes'*) that snaps instantly to flat neutral while the social beat is still open. [L2-HOOK:L2-M04-stop-vs-fade-timing]

### Mechanism B: Leakage & Upper-Face Recruits (Microexpression Leakage & Artificial Smile)
The lower face is under heavy voluntary control while the upper face (inner brows, orbicularis oculi, subtle nostril flaring) is harder to fake on command. An **Artificial Smile** pulls lip corners up while eyes stay flat; **Microexpression Leakage** flashes across the face for 1/25th to 1/5th of a second before the polite mask clamps down.

Catching a fifth-of-a-second hydraulic flash is physically impossible while your own mind is busy composing speech. To read the seam, you must deploy **Landing-Window Attention**—separating *delivery* from *observation*: place the high-salience trigger phrase at the very end of a short, clean sentence, then go completely silent. That quiet landing window frees your visual bandwidth to register the raw autonomic impulse before the subject's manual rigging can respond.

*Micro-Scenario:* Mentioning your engineering VP will co-lead a merger triggers a unilateral upper-lip contempt twitch (**Microexpression Leakage**) in the quiet landing window before an **Artificial Smile** and polite agreement override it. [L2-HOOK:L2-M04-microexpression-leakage]

### Mechanism C: Recalled vs. Constructed Accounts (Fabrication Marker)
- **Recalled Memory Pattern:** Uneven sensory details, natural self-corrections, and emotional expressions firing *before* or *simultaneously* with words.
- **Constructed Pattern (Fabrication Marker):** Elevated load above **Cognitive Baseline** (M03), emotional displays lagging *behind* verbal claims, flattened chronology, and stalling on unscripted follow-ups.

Never equate polish with deceit. A true story told five times to five stakeholders naturally sands down its own edges into a crisp, rehearsed summary (**Rehearsed Truth Artifact**). The diagnostic separator is not the polish of the initial recital—it is **elasticity under off-script pressure**. A rehearsed truth still sits atop real episodic memory and expands smoothly when probed from an unexpected angle; a constructed account has no underlying architecture to draw from, causing cognitive load to spike the moment you step off the script.

*Micro-Scenario:* A contractor delivers a hyper-clean timeline with a delayed worry expression; an off-script sensory question about the south gate breaks his cadence and freezes his blink rate. [L2-HOOK:L2-M04-fabrication-vs-recall]

sensorToActuatorLoops.title: Leakage Cross-Check
sensorToActuatorLoops.sensorInput: Microexpression Leakage or abrupt Expression Stop during an open social beat immediately following a statement delivered via Landing-Window Attention.
sensorToActuatorLoops.interpreterHypothesis: Incongruence between performed social mask and underlying autonomic reaction (hold Hypothesis Plurality—do not jump straight to deception).
sensorToActuatorLoops.actuatorCalibration: Maintain flat Operator Baseline. Do not call out the face. Cross-check against a BToE Stress Cluster (M03) and drop a calm, open-ended follow-up.
sensorToActuatorLoops.feedbackSignal: Subject either voices the real objection cleanly or exhibits a reinforcing stress cluster on the exact same topic.

sensorToActuatorLoops.title: Off-Script Memory Elasticity Probe
sensorToActuatorLoops.sensorInput: Rehearsed, hyper-clean chronology paired with delayed emotional timing (Fabrication Marker).
sensorToActuatorLoops.interpreterHypothesis: Account may be constructed/sanitized OR a Rehearsed Truth Artifact from prior retellings.
sensorToActuatorLoops.actuatorCalibration: Ask a low-threat, unexpected sensory or reverse-order detail question to test narrative elasticity.
sensorToActuatorLoops.feedbackSignal: Recalled memory adapts fluidly with minor self-corrections; constructed accounts spike cognitive load, stall, or trigger defensive withdrawal.

commonMisconceptions: 'Lie to Me' Misconception: expecting dramatic textbook microexpressions in everyday interactions.
Polite-Mask False Positive: mistaking routine professional Artificial Smiles for covert malice or deceit.
highProbabilityFalsePositives: Social-Transition Cutoff: misreading an abrupt smile drop caused by pivoting to a laptop/notebook as a dropped mask.
Rehearsed Truth Artifact: misclassifying a true story polished through repetition as a constructed cover story.
disconfirmingEvidenceRules: If a subject's facial asymmetry or flat upper face appears identically during genuine low-stakes laughter—or if an off-script sensory question is answered fluidly without cognitive stalling—your Fabrication Marker hypothesis is falsified.

secondOrder: Hyper-fixating on a subject's face to catch 1/5th-second flashes creates an unblinking stare that breaks Operator Baseline (M01) and manufactures Observer Distortion.
thirdOrder: Treating polite social masking (Artificial Smile) as covert hostility breeds chronic operator paranoia and erodes trust with tired or diplomatic allies.

L2-M04-stop-vs-fade-timing.operationalFocus: Distinguishing a performed Expression Stop (social mask dropping prematurely) from benign Social-Transition Cutoff.

workedExample.setting: Budget alignment meeting with a regional director whose team is being audited next week.
workedExample.sceneMarkdown: Announcing the audit schedule, the director pulls a wide Artificial Smile ('Honestly, I love having Finance double-check our numbers'). The exact millisecond she finishes 'numbers'—while still looking directly at you waiting for a reply—the smile snaps to flat, tight-lipped neutral with a jaw clench.

ctaLoop.baseline: Earlier genuine smiles engaged cheeks/eyes and faded organically over 2-3 seconds.
ctaLoop.deviationOrCluster: Lower-face Artificial Smile + vertical Expression Stop during an open social beat + subtle jaw clench.
ctaLoop.internalDriverHypothesis: Hypothesis Plurality: (A) Anticipates audit will uncover messy approvals; OR (B) Resents administrative drag during Q4 close.
ctaLoop.tacticalProbeOrActuator: Hold Operator Baseline and lower threat: 'I know Q4 close is brutal—if there's a vendor bucket still messy, flag it now so Finance treats it as work-in-progress instead of an exception.'
ctaLoop.observableFeedbackAndNextMove: Jaw unclenches, she exhales, and immediately flags two unapproved contractor invoices.

deceptiveNonExample.mirrorSceneMarkdown: Sharing approved headcount news, she smiles warmly ('That's huge, thank you') and half a second later her face snaps to flat, furrowed concentration.
deceptiveNonExample.benignRootCause: Social-Transition Cutoff—eyes dropped simultaneously to her open laptop to verify whether the new headcount ID is live in Workday.
deceptiveNonExample.disconfirmingCue: Initial smile recruited upper face (eyes crinkled), and the abrupt cutoff coincided directly with screen fixation rather than an open social beat.
deceptiveNonExample.falsePositiveCost: Second-guessing genuine buy-in injects unnecessary awkwardness into a smooth win.

L2-M04-microexpression-leakage.operationalFocus: Using Landing-Window Attention to catch brief upper-face/lip leakage and cross-checking without overreacting.

workedExample.setting: Partnership scoping call with a rival firm's VP of Product.
workedExample.sceneMarkdown: Placing the sensitive clause at the end of a short sentence and going silent: 'For Phase 1, our security architect will hold final veto on API changes.' In the quiet landing window, the left corner of his upper lip twitches upward in micro-contempt before a smooth nod and 'Makes total sense.'

ctaLoop.baseline: Symmetrical facial movement, relaxed mouth, engaged posture throughout earlier roadmap alignment.
ctaLoop.deviationOrCluster: Unilateral upper-lip lift (Microexpression Leakage) pinned directly to 'final veto' + immediate verbal compliance contradicting the flash.
ctaLoop.internalDriverHypothesis: Views veto clause as an insult to his engineering team's competence and plans to stall or renegotiate later.
ctaLoop.tacticalProbeOrActuator: Do not confront the face. Open a safe valve: 'I've seen veto clauses slow good teams if the turnaround SLA isn't tight. How would your engineers structure that review loop so it's not a bottleneck?'
ctaLoop.observableFeedbackAndNextMove: Polite mask drops; he leans in and voices his real objection—requesting a 24-hour SLA and shared sign-off criteria.

deceptiveNonExample.mirrorSceneMarkdown: Delivering the veto clause, the VP's left upper lip twitches briefly upward before he nods and agrees.
deceptiveNonExample.benignRootCause: Natural unilateral motor tic (Exogenous Noise)—he does the exact same lip twitch whenever swallowing or pausing to think.
deceptiveNonExample.disconfirmingCue: Identical left-lip twitch appeared twice during neutral small talk about coffee, with zero accompanying BToE Stress Cluster or vocal constriction.
deceptiveNonExample.falsePositiveCost: Reopening a settled contract clause over a baseline facial tic concedes leverage you already held.

L2-M04-fabrication-vs-recall.operationalFocus: Testing narrative elasticity under off-script sensory questioning to separate a Fabrication Marker from a Rehearsed Truth Artifact.

workedExample.setting: Internal review of a missed regulatory filing deadline with an operations coordinator.
workedExample.sceneMarkdown: Coordinator delivers a remarkably smooth, uninterrupted 30-second timeline ('Uploaded at 4:15, got confirmation banner, logged out') with a delayed look of worry appearing after saying 'I was really stressed.'

ctaLoop.baseline: Normally speaks in conversational bursts with minor pauses and natural gestures (Cognitive Baseline).
ctaLoop.deviationOrCluster: Hyper-clean rehearsed cadence + verbal-to-facial lag (Fabrication Marker).
ctaLoop.internalDriverHypothesis: Hypothesis Plurality: (A) Never completed final submission step; OR (B) Rehearsed Truth Artifact from briefing his manager earlier.
ctaLoop.tacticalProbeOrActuator: Deploy calm, off-script sensory/reverse-order probe: 'Just so IT can trace the portal bug, walk me backward from the confirmation banner: which browser were you in, and did the PDF preview load before submit?'
ctaLoop.observableFeedbackAndNextMove: Blink rate freezes, Artificial Smile flashes and stops, and he stalls before admitting the tab may still have been spinning when he closed it.

deceptiveNonExample.mirrorSceneMarkdown: Coordinator delivers the exact same polished 30-second chronological summary with zero pauses.
deceptiveNonExample.benignRootCause: Rehearsed Truth Artifact—she already walked Legal and her Director through the identical portal glitch twice that morning.
deceptiveNonExample.disconfirmingCue: Answers the off-script sensory probe fluidly ('Edge—and page 2 rendered upside down, which is why I double-checked the timestamp').
deceptiveNonExample.falsePositiveCost: Triggering the Othello Error against an honest employee destroys psychological safety.

L3-M04-facial-asymmetry-timing.externalScienceMarkdown: While posed expressions tend to show sharper onset/offset boundaries than spontaneous ones, EMG and naturalistic studies (Ross & Pulusu, 2013; Schmidt et al., 2006) reveal **spontaneous expressions are also frequently asymmetric** due to normal hemispheric motor lateralization. Timing (Stop vs. Fade) differentiates social performance better than static asymmetry, but neither is diagnostic without Subject Baseline.
L3-M04-facial-asymmetry-timing.operationalTranslation: Prioritize temporal seams (abrupt cutoff during an open social beat) over static facial asymmetry, always verified against genuine low-stakes humor.
keyReferences: Ross & Pulusu (2013) Posed vs. spontaneous facial expressions
Schmidt et al. (2006) Journal of Nonverbal Behavior

L3-M04-duchenne-smile-faking.externalScienceMarkdown: Controlled studies (Krumhuber & Manstead, 2009; Gunnery, Hall, & Ruben, 2013) show **60-70% of adults can voluntarily contract orbicularis oculi** to produce a convincing Duchenne smile on command, while genuine low-intensity amusement does not always crinkle the eyes.
L3-M04-duchenne-smile-faking.operationalTranslation: Treat a lower-face-only Artificial Smile as a soft indicator of low-effort politeness (never deception), and never assume eye-crinkling guarantees sincerity.
keyReferences: Gunnery, Hall, & Ruben (2013) Deliberate Duchenne Smile

L3-M04-microexpression-validity.externalScienceMarkdown: Porter & ten Brinke (2008) found full-face microexpressions occurred in **only ~2% of deceptive statements** and also appeared in truthful ones. Feldman Barrett et al. (2019) further established that facial muscle configurations do not map 1:1 to universal internal emotional states across contexts and cultures.
L3-M04-microexpression-validity.operationalTranslation: Discard real-time 'microexpression hunting.' Treat obvious facial-verbal incongruence strictly as a prompt to ask a calm clarifying question.

L3-M04-fabricated-memory-cues.topicTitle: Reconstructive Memory vs. Cognitive Credibility Assessment (CCA)
L3-M04-fabricated-memory-cues.externalScienceMarkdown: Memory is reconstructive (Loftus), so messy gaps do not prove deceit. While isolated facial tells like nostril flaring fail controlled testing, **unanticipated off-script spatial/temporal questions** and **verifiability checks** (Vrij et al., 2017) are empirically validated because they exploit genuine cognitive-load asymmetry between recall and invention.
L3-M04-fabricated-memory-cues.operationalTranslation: Keep the off-script verbal elasticity probe; drop facial lie-detector tells.
keyReferences: Vrij et al. (2017) Cognitive Credibility Assessment
Loftus (2005) Planting misinformation in the human mind

proposedGlossaryAdditions.definition: Placing a high-salience phrase at the end of a short prompt and going completely silent so operator visual bandwidth is free to observe the immediate 1-second autonomic response.
Misreading an abrupt drop in facial expression caused by normal cognitive task-switching (e.g., looking at a screen or notes) as a performed Expression Stop.
Misclassifying a genuine, truthful account that has been polished through repeated retelling as a constructed Fabrication Marker.
